name: Hakone
tagline: Hot springs, Mount Fuji views and a lake loop
summary: Hakone is Tokyo's favourite hot-spring escape, a volcanic mountain area with ryokan inns, open-air baths and views of Mount Fuji on clear days. A classic loop links a mountain railway, cable car, steaming volcanic valley, pirate-ship cruise on Lake Ashi and excellent art museums.
seasonNote: Autumn colours peak in November and Fuji is clearest in winter. Summer is humid and often hazy. Weekends are busy with Tokyo visitors.
arrival: The Odakyu Romancecar from Shinjuku reaches Hakone-Yumoto in about 85 minutes. The Hakone Free Pass covers the loop.
gettingAround: The Hakone Tozan railway, cable car, ropeway, lake boats and buses; the Free Pass covers all.
foodTip: Black eggs boiled in Owakudani's hot springs, tofu dishes and soba.
buyTip: Yosegi-zaiku marquetry boxes and onsen manju.
baseArea: Hakone-Yumoto, Gora or a ryokan by the lake

items.name: Lake Ashi cruise
items.summary: Replica pirate ships sail across a crater lake with Fuji views on clear days.
items.tip: Sit on the open deck facing Fuji.
items.why: The heart of the Hakone loop.

items.name: Hakone Shrine
items.summary: A shrine in cedar forest with a red torii gate standing in the lake.
items.tip: Go early for the lakeside gate.

items.name: Owakudani
items.summary: A steaming volcanic valley of sulphur vents, reached by ropeway.
items.expect: May close when volcanic activity is high.

items.name: Hakone Open-Air Museum
items.summary: Sculptures by Moore, Rodin and others set in gardens, plus a Picasso pavilion.
items.tip: Soak your feet in the footbath.

items.name: Hakone Ropeway
items.summary: Cable cars over volcanic slopes with views of Fuji and the lake.
items.tip: Ride in the morning for clear skies.

items.name: Onsen bathing
items.summary: Hot-spring baths in ryokan and day spas like Tenzan.
items.expect: Bathe nude; tattoos may be refused.
items.tip: Try a private bath if you have tattoos.

items.name: Old Tokaido road
items.summary: Stone-paved Edo-era highway through cedars, with a 400-year-old teahouse.

items.name: Black eggs
items.summary: Eggs boiled in hot springs until their shells turn black.
items.tip: Legend says each adds seven years to your life.

items.name: Tofu kaiseki
items.summary: Course meals built around local tofu and spring water.

items.name: Soba
items.summary: Handmade buckwheat noodles, hot or cold.

name: Nikko
tagline: Gilded shrines in cedar forest and mountain lakes
summary: Nikko's lavish Toshogu shrine, the mausoleum of shogun Tokugawa Ieyasu, is covered in gold leaf and carvings. Around it stand temples and shrines in ancient cedar forest, and above town the Kegon Falls, Lake Chuzenji and the Senjogahara marsh offer mountain scenery.
seasonNote: October brings famous autumn colours, starting at the lake. Spring is fresh and green. Winter is cold with snow at the lake.
arrival: Tobu limited express trains from Asakusa take about 2 hours. JR Pass users go via Utsunomiya.
gettingAround: Walk or bus between the station and shrines; buses climb the Irohazaka road to the lake.
foodTip: Yuba (tofu skin), soba and yokan sweet bean jelly.
baseArea: Near the shrines or at Lake Chuzenji

items.name: Nikko Toshogu
items.summary: A dazzling shrine of gold leaf and carvings, including the 'see no evil' monkeys.
items.tip: See the sleeping cat carving and Yomeimon gate.

items.name: Shinkyo Bridge
items.summary: A sacred red lacquered bridge over the rushing Daiya River.
items.expect: Small fee to step on it.
items.tip: Photograph it from the road bridge.

items.name: Rinno-ji
items.summary: A temple with three giant gilded Buddhas and a quiet garden.

items.name: Futarasan Shrine
items.summary: A shrine to Nikko's sacred mountains, in deep cedar forest.

items.name: Kanmangafuchi Abyss
items.summary: A riverside path lined with rows of moss-covered stone Jizo statues.
items.tip: Walk it in the morning mist.

items.name: Kegon Falls
items.summary: A 97 m waterfall dropping from Lake Chuzenji, with a lift to a viewing platform.
items.tip: Ride the lift to the base platform.
items.why: One of Japan's top three falls.

items.name: Lake Chuzenji
items.summary: A mountain lake beneath Mount Nantai, with cruises and old embassy villas.

items.name: Senjogahara marsh
items.summary: A boardwalk across a highland marsh to Yudaki falls.

items.name: Yuba
items.summary: Delicate tofu skin, served fresh, rolled or in soba and rice bowls.

items.name: Soba
items.summary: Buckwheat noodles with mountain vegetables.

items.name: Mizu-yokan
items.summary: Sweet bean jelly made with Nikko spring water.
items.expect: Old sweet shops on the main street.
items.tip: Buy a box to take home.

name: Takayama
tagline: An Edo-era mountain town of sake breweries and Hida beef
summary: Takayama in the Japanese Alps has a beautifully preserved old merchant quarter of dark wooden houses, sake breweries and morning markets. Its spring and autumn festivals feature ornate floats, and it's the gateway to the thatched farmhouses of Shirakawa-go.
seasonNote: The Takayama Festival is on 14 to 15 April and 9 to 10 October. Winter is snowy and beautiful. Summer is warm and green.
arrival: The scenic Hida limited express from Nagoya takes about 2.5 hours. Buses link Kanazawa via Shirakawa-go.
gettingAround: Walk the compact centre; buses to Shirakawa-go and the Alps.
foodTip: Hida beef sushi and skewers, Takayama ramen, mitarashi dango and local sake.
buyTip: Sarubobo dolls, Hida furniture and sake.
baseArea: Near the old town or a ryokan

items.name: Sanmachi Suji old town
items.summary: Lanes of Edo-era merchant houses, sake breweries and craft shops.
items.tip: Look for cedar balls marking breweries.

items.name: Miyagawa morning market
items.summary: A riverside market of pickles, vegetables, crafts and snacks.

items.name: Takayama Jinya
items.summary: The only surviving Edo-period government office building in Japan.

items.name: Hida Folk Village
items.summary: Open-air museum of thatched farmhouses moved from around the region.
items.tip: Visit in snow if you can.

items.name: Festival Floats Exhibition Hall
items.summary: Ornate festival floats with mechanical puppets.
items.expect: Real floats rotate through the year.

items.name: Shirakawa-go
items.summary: A village of steep thatched gassho farmhouses in a mountain valley.

items.name: Shinhotaka Ropeway

items.name: Hida beef

items.name: Takayama ramen
items.summary: Thin curly noodles in a light soy broth.

items.name: Mitarashi dango and sake

name: Yokohama
tagline: Japan's harbour city, with Kamakura's Great Buddha nearby
summary: Yokohama opened to foreign trade in 1859 and still feels cosmopolitan, with Japan's largest Chinatown, a waterfront of red-brick warehouses and a futuristic Minato Mirai skyline. It's an easy base or day trip from Tokyo, and the temples of Kamakura are close.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best. Summer is hot and humid, with fireworks over the harbour.
arrival: Trains from Tokyo take 25 to 40 minutes. Haneda Airport is 30 minutes away.
gettingAround: Minatomirai line, JR trains and waterfront walks.
foodTip: Chinatown buns and dumplings, Iekei ramen and Napolitan spaghetti, born here.

items.name: Minato Mirai waterfront
items.summary: A futuristic harbour district with a giant Ferris wheel and ship museum.

items.name: Chinatown
items.summary: Japan's largest Chinatown, packed with restaurants, temples and snack stalls.

items.name: Sankeien Garden
items.summary: A traditional garden with historic buildings, including a three-storey pagoda.
items.tip: Visit in plum or autumn season.

items.name: Cup Noodles Museum
items.summary: A playful museum where you design your own cup noodles.

items.name: Red Brick Warehouse
items.summary: Restored customs warehouses of shops and events.
items.tip: Visit in December for the Christmas market.

items.name: Landmark Tower Sky Garden
items.summary: A 69th-floor observation deck with views to Mount Fuji.
items.tip: Go on a clear winter day.

items.name: Kamakura Great Buddha
items.summary: A 13 m bronze Buddha in the open air, plus temples and a beach town.

items.name: Chinatown buns
items.summary: Steamed pork buns and soup dumplings from street windows.

items.name: Iekei ramen
items.summary: Rich pork-and-soy ramen with spinach and nori, invented here.

items.name: Napolitan spaghetti
items.summary: Ketchup spaghetti with sausage and peppers, created at the Hotel New Grand.
items.tip: Try it at the Hotel New Grand.

name: Nagoya
tagline: Castle, trains, Toyota and a bold local food scene
summary: Japan's fourth city sits between Tokyo and Kyoto on the Shinkansen. It has a golden-dolphin castle, the sacred Atsuta Shrine, great museums of trains and industry, Ghibli Park, and its own strongly flavoured food culture.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best. Summer is very hot and humid.
arrival: Shinkansen from Tokyo take about 1 hour 40 minutes; Kyoto is 35 minutes. Chubu Centrair Airport is 30 minutes by train.
gettingAround: Subway lines and the Meguru loop bus.
foodTip: Hitsumabushi eel, miso katsu, tebasaki wings and kishimen noodles.
buyTip: Arimatsu tie-dye, Noritake china and Toyota goods.

items.name: Nagoya Castle
items.summary: A castle with golden dolphins on the roof and a rebuilt Hommaru Palace.
items.expect: The main keep is closed for rebuilding; the palace is open.

items.name: Atsuta Shrine
items.summary: One of Shinto's most important shrines, said to hold a sacred sword.

items.name: SCMaglev and Railway Park
items.summary: Shinkansen, maglev and steam trains you can walk through.

items.name: Toyota Industry and Technology Museum
items.wiki: Toyota Commemorative Museum of Industry and Technology
items.summary: Looms to cars in an old red-brick factory, with live demonstrations.

items.name: Osu Kannon and shopping street
items.summary: A temple next to arcades of vintage shops, electronics and street food.
items.expect: Monthly flea market on the 18th and 28th.
items.tip: Eat your way down the arcade.

items.name: Tokugawa Art Museum
items.summary: Treasures of the Owari Tokugawa lords, including Tale of Genji scrolls.

items.name: Ghibli Park

items.name: Inuyama Castle

items.name: Hitsumabushi
items.summary: Grilled eel over rice, eaten three ways: plain, with condiments, then with broth.

items.name: Miso katsu
items.summary: Pork cutlet in thick red miso sauce.

items.name: Tebasaki wings

name: Kobe
tagline: A port city of Kobe beef, mountains and nearby Himeji Castle
summary: Kobe sits between the sea and the Rokko mountains. It's home to world-famous beef, a waterfront of towers and parks, foreign merchants' houses in Kitano, and hot springs at Arima. Himeji Castle, Japan's finest, is a short train ride away.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are ideal. The Kobe Luminarie light festival is in December. Summer is hot and humid.
arrival: Shin-Kobe station is on the Shinkansen. Trains from Osaka take about 25 minutes.
gettingAround: JR, Hankyu and Hanshin trains, the subway and city loop buses.
foodTip: Kobe beef teppanyaki, Chinatown snacks, akashiyaki and sobameshi.
buyTip: Kobe sweets, pearls and sake from the Nada district.

items.name: Meriken Park and Port Tower
items.summary: A red lattice tower and harbour park with the earthquake memorial.
items.tip: Visit at night when it's lit.

items.name: Kitano Ijinkan
items.summary: Western-style houses built by 19th-century foreign merchants on a hillside.
items.expect: Many houses charge separately; pick a few.

items.name: Nunobiki Falls and Herb Gardens
items.summary: Waterfalls a short walk from the Shinkansen station, and a ropeway to herb gardens.
items.tip: Ride the ropeway down at dusk.

items.name: Mount Rokko night view
items.summary: Mountain views over Kobe and Osaka Bay, among Japan's best night views.

items.name: Ikuta Shrine
items.summary: One of Japan's oldest shrines, in the middle of downtown.

items.name: Arima Onsen
items.summary: An ancient hot-spring town known for its gold and silver waters.

items.name: Himeji Castle
items.summary: Japan's finest original castle, a white 'heron' on its hill.

items.name: Kobe beef teppanyaki

items.name: Nankinmachi Chinatown

items.name: Akashiyaki and sobameshi

name: Nagasaki
tagline: A hillside harbour city of peace, trade and churches
summary: For two centuries Nagasaki was Japan's only window to the West, and its Dutch, Chinese and Portuguese influences still shape its churches, food and streets. The Peace Park and Atomic Bomb Museum are deeply moving, and the abandoned island of Gunkanjima lies offshore.
seasonNote: Spring and autumn are best. Summer is hot and rainy. The Lantern Festival brightens February.
arrival: The Nishi-Kyushu Shinkansen and relay trains from Fukuoka take about 1.5 hours. Nagasaki Airport is 45 minutes by bus.
gettingAround: Old trams cover the main sights cheaply.
foodTip: Champon noodles, castella sponge cake and Turkish rice.

connections.note: Shinkansen with a change at Takeo-Onsen.

items.name: Peace Park and Hypocentre
items.summary: The Peace Statue and the hypocentre of the 9 August 1945 atomic bomb.

items.name: Atomic Bomb Museum
items.summary: A moving museum of the bombing and its aftermath.
items.expect: Allow 1.5 hours; some exhibits are graphic.
items.tip: Visit the memorial hall next door.

items.name: Glover Garden
items.summary: Hillside Western houses of 19th-century merchants with harbour views.
items.tip: Visit at night for lit-up views.

items.name: Oura Church
items.summary: Japan's oldest standing church, where hidden Christians revealed themselves in 1865.
items.tip: Read the story of the hidden Christians.

items.name: Dejima
items.summary: The rebuilt Dutch trading post, Japan's only link to Europe for 200 years.

items.name: Gunkanjima
items.summary: 'Battleship Island', an abandoned coal-mining island of concrete ruins.

items.name: Mount Inasa night view
items.summary: A ropeway to one of Japan's top three night views.

items.name: Megane Bridge

items.expect: Look for heart-shaped stones on the bank.

items.name: Champon
items.summary: Thick noodles in a pork and seafood broth with vegetables.

items.name: Castella
items.summary: A sponge cake brought by the Portuguese in the 16th century.
items.tip: Buy a box as a gift.

items.name: Turkish rice
